subject: Throughput allocation and tail-latency carveout request — Orion BioSystems
messages:
From: Anna Huber <anna.huber@orionbio.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: throughput allocation & tail-latency impact on reserved pool

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier this week. We ran an extended test of our variant-calling pipeline on the reserved pool you provisioned and are seeing recurring tail-latency spikes during our nightly batch windows (01:00–05:00 PST). The pattern: long-context genomics requests (mean sequence length ~5k tokens) cause queueing that pushes latency for our interactive tasks above acceptable levels.

Summary:
- Workload: mix of long-batched inference jobs and short interactive steps (~80% batch, 20% interactive).
- Impact: interactive P95 latency jumps to ~1.2s during batch runs; baseline P95 is ~240ms.
- Our ask: a carveout or queueing exception so our interactive routes are given higher priority, or an SLA amendment guaranteeing a throughput floor for interactive traffic during nightly windows. We can tolerate slightly higher cost if it means stable p95.

Attached: orion_perf_snapshot_q1-2026.xlsx (perf counters, sequence distribution, traces).

Can Redwood propose an operational solution (reserved carveout, preemption limits, or pinned fraction of GPUs) plus an amended SLA for the next 90 days while we stabilize? We’d like to have an agreement in place before our next production run on Jan 28.

Best,
Anna Huber
Head of Platform Engineering
Orion BioSystems

---

Hi Anna,

Appreciate the detailed snapshot — that helps a lot. We can definitely explore a short-term operational carveout to protect interactive routes during your nightly batch windows. Quick questions to scope the engineering change:

- Which routes/endpoints need the priority carveout? (route names or API keys)
- Target p95 for interactive traffic you need during the window (what is acceptable?)
- Are you OK with a temporary model variant fallback (smaller quantized model) for long-batched jobs if we need hard isolation?

Internally I’ll loop in our SRE and product ops to evaluate options (pin fraction of GPUs, queue-key priority, or timeboxed queue exemptions). I’ll aim to get an initial proposal by EOD Friday. If you’re available, let’s book a quick sync on Jan 18 to go over the proposal.

Thanks,

Subject: Fwd: Request: throughput allocation & tail-latency impact on reserved pool

Marissa / Laura — forwarding Orion’s perf dump and their ask. TL;DR: they want either a queueing exception for interactive routes during 01:00–05:00 PST nightly windows or an SLA amendment guaranteeing p95 bounds for interactive traffic. They are willing to accept higher unit cost for that window.

Proposed options from a product/ops perspective:
- Option A: Pin 20% of their reserved capacity (e.g., 8 GPUs -> pin 2 GPUs) for interactive queue keys at all times. Guarantees isolation but reduces batch throughput.
- Option B: Timeboxed queueing carveout (01:00–05:00) where preemption thresholds are disabled for their priority keys — cheaper but higher operational complexity.
- Option C: Model fallback for batch jobs during windows (quantized / smaller variant) to reduce tail latency without carving capacity.

Key questions for SRE: cost/operational risk of Option B (requires changes to the scheduler and playbook), telemetry we’d need to commit to (per-route p95/p99, queue depth logs), and whether we can offer a temporary SLA amendment for 90 days with weekly reporting.

Anna’s original email attached below.

— Jonas

Jonas / Marissa,

We can support a timeboxed carveout (Option B) but there are a few caveats and required controls:

1) Operational changes: SRE will need a playbook (runbook) and a short maintenance window to update the scheduler rules — I’ve attached a draft playbook that outlines the rollback and monitoring steps.

2) Telemetry & SLA language: We can offer a 90-day temporary amendment that guarantees interactive route P95 <= 500ms for the 01:00–05:00 window, subject to the following telemetry being enabled by Orion: per-route traces, token counts, and queue-depth logs shipped to our ingest for the duration of the amendment. If the telemetry is incomplete we cannot validate SLA compliance.

3) Safety limits: To avoid starvation, we’ll enforce a max pin of 30% of the pool or a hard cap of 3 GPUs (whichever lower). If Orion needs >3 GPUs pinned we’d have to convert to a dedicated carveout SKU which changes pricing and contract.

4) Fallback: Option C (fallback model for batch) is low-risk and recommended as a complement. If Orion can run a quantized variant for non-interactive tasks during the window we can keep costs lower and avoid scheduler churn.

I’ve cc’d SRE lead (ops on-call) offline. If we proceed, we’ll need a signed amendment and access to Orion’s telemetry endpoints by Jan 26 to meet the Jan 28 rollout.

Laura Bennett
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Throughput allocation and tail-latency carveout request — Orion BioSystems

Hi Anna —

Thanks for your patience. Following internal review, here’s the proposed path forward we can commit to for a 90-day trial:

1) Operational carveout window: Redwood will enable a timeboxed queueing exception for the priority route keys you specify between 01:00–05:00 PST daily. During that window we will suspend global preemption for those keys and route them to a capped pinned fraction of the pool.

2) Capacity & limits: We can pin up to 3 GPUs for interactive traffic (capped at 30% of the provisioned pool). If Orion requires more than 3 pinned GPUs we will switch to a dedicated carveout SKU and update pricing.

3) SLA metrics: Temporary amendment will guarantee interactive route P95 <= 500ms during the carveout window, validated by the telemetry below. This is for 90 days starting on the rollout date.

4) Telemetry requirements: Orion must enable per-route traces, token counts, and queue-depth logs to the agreed ingest endpoint. Weekly compliance reports will be produced by Redwood; failure to provide telemetry voids the SLA guarantees.

5) Fallback recommendation: We strongly recommend combining the carveout with a quantized fallback for long-batched jobs (Option C) to reduce operational risk and cost.

Next steps:
- I’ve attached a draft SLA amendment (sla-amendment-draft.pdf) and the operational playbook (proposed_operational_playbook.docx).
- Please review and sign the amendment (DocuSign link below) if acceptable.
- We’ll schedule a Jan 28 10:00 AM PST rollout call to validate telemetry and run a smoke test.
